issues.title: Velvet Signal — Maker Desk Draft
issues.dek: Local models are becoming first-class citizens in agent tooling — and the default network bindings of inference servers are the quiet security detail most builders skip.
editorial: The through-line across this week's packets is that wiring a local model into an agent stack has stopped being a hack. CSGLite positions itself as a lightweight local inference platform where a single command downloads a model, starts a server, and opens a chat session, with models staying loaded until you stop them manually and optional CSGHub access tokens for private models (M-SRC-1). QwenPaw makes the same bet from the assistant side: if you run local models — QwenPaw Local, Ollama, or LM Studio — no API keys or cloud services are required at all (M-SRC-5).

oh-my-pi shows how far the custom-provider pattern has spread: beyond built-in Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, and vLLM local backends, you can define any OpenAI-compatible endpoint in ~/.omp/agent/models.yml, specifying baseUrl, an apiKey placeholder, and per-model contextWindow and maxTokens values — their example configures MiniMax M3 with a 100000-token context window and 32000 max tokens (M-SRC-4).

The security note worth pinning above your desk: inference servers do not agree on a safe default bind address. Per the hermes-agent provider docs, Ollama, LM Studio, and llama-server all default to 127.0.0.1, while vLLM already binds to 0.0.0.0 — all interfaces — out of the box (M-SRC-2). If you flip a local server to 0.0.0.0 to reach it from another machine — OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 for Ollama, "Serve on Network" in LM Studio's Developer tab, or --host 0.0.0.0 for llama-server — you are exposing an unauthenticated inference endpoint to your network. Check what vLLM is already doing before you assume your setup is loopback-only.

One configuration detail that saves an afternoon: when hermes configures a custom endpoint via `hermes model`, it prompts for context length and auto-detects if you leave it blank — but their documented examples set it explicitly (qwen3.5:27b at 64000, deepseek-r1:70b at 65536). Manual setting is the fix when auto-detection gets a custom endpoint wrong (M-SRC-2).
issues.pullquote: vLLM binds to 0.0.0.0 by default. Your other local servers don't. Know which one you're running before you assume your model is loopback-only.

In the hermes-agent provider configuration, Ollama, LM Studio, and llama-server default to binding 127.0.0.1, while vLLM already binds to 0.0.0.0 by default.

To expose a local inference server on the network: set OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0 for Ollama, enable "Serve on Network" in LM Studio's Developer tab → Server settings, or add --host 0.0.0.0 to the llama-server startup command.

`hermes model` prompts for context length when configuring a custom endpoint and auto-detects it if left blank; documented example models include qwen3.5:27b with context_length 64000 and deepseek-r1:70b with context_length 65536.

QwenPaw can run LLMs entirely on a local machine with no API keys or cloud services when using QwenPaw Local, Ollama, or LM Studio; tools needing extra keys (e.g. TAVILY_API_KEY for web search) are configured via Console Settings → Environment variables.

The broader ecosystem of LLM agent frameworks remains active, with the awesome-llm-agents curated list last updated 2026-08-23; Flowise (55,384 stars) is marked archived as of 2026-08, while SuperAGI, OpenAgents (XLang), and Agent Protocol appear with their listed licenses and update dates.

issues.title: The Sleep Reset: Small Habits, Honest Variance
issues.dek: A federal sleep guide offers practical, non-judgmental steps for better rest — and a reminder that what 'enough' means varies from person to person.
editorial: Sleep is often the first thing busy people squeeze out of their schedules, according to the National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI). Their guidance reframes the trade: making time to sleep may help protect your health and well-being now and in the future, and with enough sleep each night you may find you're happier and more productive during the day. [W-SRC-2]

The mechanics matter here. NHLBI explains that internal body clocks running on roughly 24-hour cycles — regulated by light, darkness, and sleep schedules — govern when you're awake and when your body is ready for sleep. Once asleep, you cycle through sleep stages in a predictable pattern. [W-SRC-5]

One concrete, evidence-backed habit: power down devices. Artificial light from screens — phones, laptops, televisions — can signal the brain that it's time to be awake, and NHLBI-funded research has linked smartphone use before bed with shorter sleep duration and worse sleep quality. Experts cited by NHLBI suggest powering down at least 30 minutes before getting into bed. [W-SRC-3]

Naps get a nuanced treatment rather than a blanket rule. NHLBI notes that daytime napping may boost alertness and performance, but if you have trouble falling asleep at night, it may help to limit naps or take them earlier in the afternoon — and adults should nap for no more than 20 minutes. [W-SRC-2]

The honest caveat: individual sleep needs vary. NHLBI itself distinguishes between the sleep needed to feel awake and the sleep needed to be healthy. [W-SRC-4] This edition offers general guidance from a public-health source, not a diagnosis or a substitute for professional care — if you suspect a sleep disorder such as insomnia or sleep apnea, NHLBI's resources cover these conditions and point toward professional evaluation. [W-SRC-1]
issues.pullquote: Sleep is often the first thing that busy people squeeze out of their schedules. [W-SRC-2]

issues.title: The Leftover Ledger: A Calm Guide to What Keeps and What Goes
issues.dek: USDA cold-storage windows, the two-hour rule, and a weekly fridge ritual — practical guidance for leftovers without guesswork.
editorial: Leftovers are one of the most common points of kitchen uncertainty: the container in the back of the fridge with no label and no story. The USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service offers unusually clear, specific guidance here — not vague warnings, but actual day counts for cooked leftovers, raw meats, deli items, and more. This edition turns those numbers into a practical rhythm for your kitchen.

The core numbers are simple. Cooked leftovers keep 3 to 4 days in the refrigerator or 3 to 4 months in the freezer (P-SRC-2). Raw poultry and ground meats are shorter-lived: 1 to 2 days in the fridge (P-SRC-1). Deli salads, store-cooked entrees, and casseroles fall in the 3-to-5-day range (P-SRC-1). These are validity windows, not judgment calls — when the storage history is unknown, the guidance is to discard rather than guess.

The two-hour rule is the other anchor. Perishable food left at room temperature longer than 2 hours should be discarded — 1 hour if the room is above 90°F (P-SRC-3). Above 40°F and below 140°F is the 'Danger Zone' where bacteria multiply quickly (P-SRC-4). Reheat leftovers to 165°F, checking with a thermometer in several places (P-SRC-4).

Cooling matters as much as storage. Divide large batches — soup, roasts, turkey — into shallow containers or smaller pieces so food reaches 40°F or below quickly (P-SRC-2). Wrap well or use airtight containers to keep bacteria out and moisture in (P-SRC-2).

Finally, a weekly ritual: once a week, go through the fridge and discard perishables past their window (P-SRC-1). An open box of baking soda on a shelf keeps things smelling fresh (P-SRC-1). This is not alarmism — it is a small, repeatable habit that replaces uncertainty with a known answer.
issues.pullquote: Cooked leftovers: 3 to 4 days refrigerated, 3 to 4 months frozen. Raw poultry and ground meats: 1 to 2 days. When the clock is unknown, discard — don't guess.

issues.title: Aura Farming: The Charisma Contest That Walked Off the Screen
issues.dek: A TikTok-born ritual of poses and references has moved into the streets — and its meaning is still up for grabs.
editorial: "Aura farming" started as a TikTok meme and has grown into a kind of street-level contest: two people face off, cycling through poses, gestures, and references, and the crowd decides who has more "aura" — an unspoken blend of charisma, style, and self-confidence [C-SRC-1].

What makes it interesting is how much of the game is legible only to insiders. To an outsider, the performances can look like nonsense; to participants, spotting the references is the point [C-SRC-1]. The Spanish-language variant "farmear aura" shows the format traveling across languages [C-SRC-1].

We're not going to tell you what "aura" universally means — the term is doing different work in different corners of the internet, and the packets don't settle it. What we can say: it's a competition format, it rewards performative cool, and it's currently visible enough that it's crossing from feeds into physical spaces [C-SRC-1].
If you've seen it and felt out of the loop, that's not a gap in your cultural knowledge — the in-group legibility is a designed feature of the format, not a bug [C-SRC-1].
issues.pullquote: "For the participants, spotting the references is part of the game."

issues.title: Velvet Signal — Maker Desk: Proposed Edition
issues.kicker: vLLM's Transformers v5 pivot and a new auth surface for /v2 endpoints
issues.dek: The week's most consequential builder change: vLLM now targets Transformers v5, and its OpenAI-compatible /v2 endpoints gained API-key authorization. Both touch deployment and security posture directly.
editorial: vLLM's latest release shifts the project to target Transformers v5, with vendored MiniCPM-V/O processors and compatibility fixes for Sarvam and Voxtral (M-SRC-3). If you pin Transformers in your serving stack, this is the release to test against before it tests you.

The multi-tier KV cache offloading framework grew an object-store secondary tier, HMA is now enabled by default for capable connectors, tiering support landed for HMA models, and a per-request offloading policy is available via the on_new_request lifecycle hook (M-SRC-3). Offloading is moving from an optimization to a first-class architecture.

On the frontend: configurable truncation side for OpenAI endpoints, normalization of reasoning_content to reasoning, a reworked fastokens integration, consolidated Speech-to-Text entrypoints, beam-search consolidation via BeamSearchMixin, and score/rerank chat-template instructions (M-SRC-3).
Security note worth acting on: API-key authorization for /v2 endpoints landed in this release (M-SRC-3). If you expose /v2, review your auth configuration as part of upgrading.

Offline API restructuring: the pooling offline API was split into PoolingOfflineMixin, and offline inference APIs/utils were split (M-SRC-3). Import paths may have moved — check before upgrading scripts that call these directly.
